page: Vultr vcg-a16-24c-256g-64vram is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For hardware acceleration, it integrates four NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results show average multi-core CPU performance with a stress-ng multi-core score of 41473.88 and a Passmark CPU score of 35340.23. The memory subsystem achieves a read-only large block bandwidth of 137.58 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 56.27 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds, reaching 8464.24 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 614.8 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are strong, registering at 32.83 tokens/sec for the 7B model.

This server offers a high-density GPU configuration, bundling multiple accelerators with a large memory footprint and fast NVMe storage, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring parallel processing without the expense of top-tier enterprise training GPUs. The hardware profile is suited for high-density virtual desktop infrastructure, video transcoding, medium-scale LLM inference, and parallelized graphics rendering workloads.
